parentIntro: The last week of Term 3 — no new concept. This week sweeps back across everything since July: place value, partitioning, fact families, add/sub strategies, equal groups, division and fractions, and the big-number bridge. The app leans the questions towards whatever she's found tricky, so it will look different each day.
watchFor: This is the week to notice how much has changed since July — say it out loud to her. If something from early in the term has gone rusty, that's completely normal and exactly what this week is for; it is not a sign anything has gone wrong. Anything still shaky here is worth a mention at the next check-in.

demo.title: Look how far you've come
demo.say: No new maths today. Instead, let's look at what you could do in July, and what you can do now.

steps.caption: where we started — place value to 1000
steps.say: Back in July we were building three digit numbers out of blocks. Hundreds, tens and ones.

steps.caption: …and now you read thousands
steps.say: Now you read numbers into the thousands, and you know what every single digit is worth.

steps.caption: the take-aways that used to be scary
steps.say: And these big take-aways — the ones that felt tricky at the start of term — you have three different roads through them now.

steps.caption: one term, all of that
steps.say: That is a whole term of getting stronger. This week we just play with all of it.

weDo.problem: Pick any number between 100 and 1000 — Harriet chooses. Then pull it apart every way you can.
weDo.model: Let her choose the number (ownership matters this week). Whiteboard, no rules — just collect as many true statements about it as you can.
steps: She picks a number, say 465. Write it big.
Collect facts together: 400 + 60 + 5 · 46 tens and 5 ones · 100 more is 565 · 10 less is 455 · half of it is a bit more than 200.
Ask for the trickiest one she can think of herself — let her set you a challenge back.
No answers to check here. The aim is fluency and confidence, not a correct response.
weDo.answer: Open ended — as many true statements as she can make

weDo.problem: The two roads, one last time: 253 − 147.
weDo.model: Empty number line. Ask her to choose the road BEFORE doing any arithmetic.
steps: Ask: “count up, or jump back? Which suits these two numbers?” (They're closish, so counting up is neat.)
Ask her to explain her choice of road to you, in her own words. That explanation is the real goal of the term.
